categories.title: Origins · the wolf and the first dogs
categories.blurb: Where the dog came from: the gray wolf, the landraces that followed people out of Asia, and the breeds that still look like the animal they descend from.

categories.title: Herding · dogs that move a flock
categories.blurb: The working dogs of the sheep hill and the cattle yard: they gather, drive and hold stock, and most of them still need a job to be calm.

categories.title: Hound · nose and speed
categories.blurb: Two very different hunting methods in one shelf: the scent hounds that follow a line on the ground, and the sighthounds that run what they see.

categories.title: Working · guard, haul and rescue
categories.blurb: The heavy end of the species: sled dogs, mountain rescue dogs, water dogs and the guarding breeds that were built to hold a gate.

categories.title: Terrier · small dogs with a job
categories.blurb: Earth dogs and ratters: bred small enough to follow quarry underground, and still convinced they are the largest animal in the garden.

categories.title: Toy · companions bred small
categories.blurb: The lap dogs: bred down from working and temple dogs until the whole animal fits on a cushion, with the temperament left intact.

categories.title: Sporting · gundogs
categories.blurb: The shooting dogs of Britain and the continent: pointers that freeze, setters that range, spaniels that flush and retrievers that bring it back.

categories.title: Non-sporting · the rest of the club
categories.blurb: The utility shelf: breeds that guard, pull, sit on laps or simply refuse to be classified, from the French Bulldog to the Shiba Inu.

categories.title: Europe · breeds of the continent
categories.blurb: Britain, Germany, Switzerland and the Low Countries: the herders, guards and terriers that became the world's most widely kept dogs.

categories.title: Asia · breeds of the east
categories.blurb: Japan, China, Afghanistan and the Fertile Crescent: the spitz breeds of the north, the flat-faced companions of the palaces and the desert sighthounds.

categories.title: Africa · breeds of the continent
categories.blurb: From the Atlas to the Cape: the Basenji, the ridgeback and the landraces that never needed a kennel club to survive.

categories.title: Americas · breeds of the new world
categories.blurb: Canada, the United States and the working farms of the continent: sled dogs, water dogs and the farm ratters bred after the frontier closed.
